name: Cacodaemon Swarm
body:
Cacodaemon Swarm
CR 11

A dizzying horde of gnashing, fleshy orbs fills the air, only a feast on their simple minds.

XP 12,800
NE Tiny outsider (daemon, evil, extraplanar, swarm)
Init +4; Senses darkvision 60 ft., detect good, detect magic; Perception +31

DEFENSE

AC 17, touch 13, flat-footed 16 (+1 dodge, +4 natural, +2 size)
hp 157 (21d10+42); fast healing 15
Fort +10, Ref +14, Will +15
Defensive Abilities swarm traits; DR 5/good or silver; Immune acid, death effects, disease, poison; Resist cold 10, electricity 10, fire 10

OFFENSE

Speed 5 ft., fly 50 ft. (perfect)
Melee swarm (5d6 plus disease and distraction)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 0 ft.
Special Attacks distraction (DC 23), soul lock
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 11th; concentration +12)

Constant—detect good, detect magic
At will—invisibility (self only), lesser confusion (DC 14)
3/day— commune

STATISTICS

Str 12, Dex 11, Con 13, Int 8, Wis 13, Cha 12
Base Atk +21; CMB +20; CMD 31 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Ability Focus (disease, distraction, lesser confusion), Dodge, Great Fortitude, Improved Initiative, Improved Lightning Reflexes, Iron Will, Lightning Reflexes, Skill Focus (Perception), Toughness
Skills Bluff +25, Fly +36, Knowledge (planes) +23, Perception +31, Stealth +32
Languages Abyssal, Common, Infernal; telepathy 100 ft.
SQ change shape (lizard, octopus, small scorpion or venomous snake, polymorph)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Disease (Su)

Cacodaemonia: Bite—injury; save Fortitude DC 23; onset 1 day; frequency 1/day; effect 1d2 Wisdom damage; cure 2 consecutive saves. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Soul Lock (Su)

A cacodaemon swarm can ingest the spirit of any sentient creature that has died within the last minute. This works like a cacodaemon’s soul lock ability, except both ingesting and regurgitating the gem is a free action and the ability’s use is unlimited.

ECOLOGY

Environment any (Abaddon)
Organization solitary, pair, or flood (3–10)
Treasure standard

Cacodaemons number among the weakest of their kind. Despite that, they form an incredibly important pillar of the daemon society. While many of these fiends have abilities that allow them to feed off souls and nearly all of them consider such matter a great delicacy, cacodaemons are one of the very few types of daemons able to actually catch a soul and solidify it into a portable form. This, along with their great numbers, makes them greatly important to their plane’s economy in the role of harvesters. Whenever a daemon would kill a mortal creature, it would also benefit greatly from the presence of these dim-witted orbs to gather its victim’s soul, be it for food, trade or other, more unspeakable purposes. This need increases rapidly with the amount of death such daemon deals, and most powerful fiends eagerly gather hordes of pet cacodaemons to fill their treasuries with incredibly potent and delicious gems they regurgitate. Such hordes are often kept together in poor conditions, let out as a ravenous swarm only when there comes a need for a harvest, falling upon their master’s slaves or opponents like flying piranhas, tearing and devouring flesh and leaving only piles of shining gems coated in blood.

Occasionally, cacodaemons band together of their own volition, seeking both safety and overwhelming offensive capabilities in numbers. Such alliances are often short?lived, as these violent and self-serving beasts don’t cooperate all too well even with their own kind, but while it lasts, a cacodaemon swarm can sometimes ward off not only mortal opponents or forces of good, but even more powerful daemons seeking to bring these soul-suckers into servitude. These independent cacodaemon swarms still create soul gems, but unlike those serving under more powerful masters, they most often devour their creations immediately in their gluttony.

While individually not that dangerous, dozens of cacodaemons banded together can pose a serious danger even to skilled combatants, and their aerial agility and speed means there is seldom a chance of escape if the combat turns sour. Those who do manage to escape quickly learn that the mind-ravaging disease that cacodaemons normally spread with their bites assaults the body much harder when brought on by a hundred of bites, and even tough creatures might succumb to madness in the wake of escaping a cacodaemon swarm.

This hulking, hunched devil is encased in a thick breastplate and wields a star-shaped axe. It lets a bellowing laugh out of its goateed face, its horns waving menacingly.
